title: Check gradients before trusting backpropagation
description: A quick reference for actual probe spacing, smoothness limits, sampled gradient evidence, and scale-aware error.

terms.definition: A materially separate sampled numerical cross-check of an analytic derivative; agreement is evidence for the selected case, not proof of the complete gradient.
A three-point derivative estimate that weights the left and right slopes using the actual rounded probe spacings.
An approximate local slope obtained by perturbing and reevaluating a function.
A derivative candidate produced by calculus or a backward implementation.
The positive value requested before floating-point rounding chooses the two representable probe locations.
The distance from the checked point to one representable probe; the left and right distances can differ.
The requirement that the derivative exists and the function is sufficiently smooth across the probe interval; passing samples do not establish it.
Approximation error remaining because the derivative uses a finite step.
Error introduced when finite-precision arithmetic stores and subtracts nearby values.
Gradient disagreement normalized by one or the larger compared magnitude.
The maximum scaled disagreement allowed before a gradient check fails.
Selecting reproducible tensor coordinates without randomness or hidden mutable state.
